extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, in-house counsel, IP owners, and clients seeking patent infringement analysis or expert services
extracted.subtask_description: Producing claim charts that map each asserted patent claim element to features of an accused product or service, with supporting evidence and a plan to resolve any gaps, to support patent litigation or licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element-by-element infringement proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent infringement must be proven by showing that the product or service infringes each and every element of the asserted claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim charts must demonstrate alleged infringement on an element-by-element basis; failure to map any element means the infringement is not truly demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual and graphical comparison (mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrating an alleged unpermitted use is a textual and graphical comparison of the claims and the potentially infringing use. Because claim charts navigate the features of the product or service using claim terms, the explained potential infringement is often referred to as a 'mapping.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both text and graphics to show how claim terms correspond to product/service features; structure mappings around claim term language so reviewers can follow the comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-column claim chart format
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'two-column' claim chart focuses on consistently mapping each claim element to a feature of the allegedly infringing product or service along with a citation to where that evidence can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each claim element include (1) the claim language and (2) the corresponding accused product/service feature plus a citation to supporting evidence (e.g., manual, spec, webpage, test result).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-column claim chart format (specification support)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'three-column' claim chart includes element-by-element cited support from the patent's specification that explains the interpretation of one or more of the claim terms and corroborates the rationale of why the cited evidence actually does demonstrate that claim element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a column with patent specification citations and explanatory text that interprets claim terms and links spec language to the accused feature and external evidence; this corroborates why the evidence satisfies the element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite evidence sources for each mapped element
rubrics_metrics.description: Mapping each claim element must be accompanied by a citation to where that evidence can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite documentation, manuals, webpages, test results, teardown findings, or other sources for every mapped element so the mapping is verifiable and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and address mapping gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Claim Chart has a 'gap' in the mapping, the alleged infringement is not truly demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where documentation is limited, perform reverse engineering and testing to fill gaps; until presence is demonstrated by RE/testing/uncovered documentation, the chart must articulate a rationale for inferring the element's presence and propose a plan to complete the mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reverse engineering, testing, and teardown to support mappings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reverse engineering and testing may be required to fill in one or more 'gaps' in the mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ reverse engineering, teardown, lab testing, and evidence-of-use analysis as methods to uncover or confirm features of the accused product/service when documentation alone is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation-ready standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Calling a claim chart 'litigation-ready' indicates that there is a high level of support in the patent specification and in the documentation of the targeted use case, but it does not typically mean it’s the streamlined version to be shown to the judge or jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A litigation-ready chart should have robust support and documentation for mappings and be suitable for driving litigation strategy (the backbone of a potential case), though it may include exhaustive detail rather than jury-presentable summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with client and counsel to leave no element unmapped without plan
rubrics_metrics.description: We work with the client and counsel to produce Claim Charts that demonstrate a likely case of infringement and aims to leave no claim element unmapped without a proper plan to complete the mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with counsel and the client to gather needed evidence, agree on claim term interpretations, and document any outstanding work and timelines to finish mapping every element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim charts guide and drive litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim Charts are generally built to guide and drive the impending litigation. The demonstrated infringement is intended to be the backbone of a potential patent case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design charts not only to document mappings but also to inform litigation strategy, including which elements are strong, where proof is needed, and how to prioritize further investigation or expert work.
